Confirmed. On the pristine tree both `should not unnecessarily reorder children #2895` and the flaky events test fail; with the fix, the memo reorder test passes and only the pre-existing focus-event flake remains (it passes in isolation).

## Summary

The fix is in `src/diff/children.js:270-279`. The `ChildReorder.reorderChildren` helper (added in #2813) recursively reorders children of function-typed vnodes, but when recursing into a component vnode it discarded the returned `_oldDom` pointer. Since memo'd components bail out of re-rendering (`newVNode._children === oldVNode._children`), their subtree takes this reorder path — and losing the resume-DOM pointer caused all following siblings to be placed at the wrong positions, scrambling the child order.

The fix propagates the returned DOM position back so sibling placement continues from the correct node:

```js
this._oldDom = new createVNode.ChildReorder(
	this._parentDom,
	this._oldDom
).reorderChildren(vnode);
```

This matches the upstream fix (preactjs/preact#2896). Verified: 916/917 karma tests pass (the one failure is a pre-existing focus-event flake in headless Chrome, unrelated), plus 27 mocha node/shared tests pass.
